preamble: The shift from 's' to 'th' (θ) is a dentalization process known as Ceceo in Spanish dialects, where sibilant alveolar fricatives are replaced by dental fricatives.

examples.note: Andalusian ceceo: /s/ is realized as a dental non-sibilant fricative, merging with /θ/.
Old Burmese s became the dental fricative [θ] (often [t̪͡θ]); the old affricate series took over [s]

sources: Hualde, J. I. (2005). The Sounds of Spanish. Cambridge University Press.
Okell, J. (1969). A Reference Grammar of Colloquial Burmese. Oxford University Press.

Rankin, R. L., Carter, R. T., Jones, A. W., Koontz, J. E., Rood, D. S., & Hartmann, I. (Eds.) (2015). Comparative Siouan Dictionary. Leipzig: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. https://csd.clld.org/
